description:
REPORTED BY USER, 2026-09-12: "Swapping does NOT swap for that day's exercise. It adds on the bottom and is not a real swap."

CONFIRMED IN CODE. swapTo (apps/web/src/screens/session/SessionScreen.tsx:321-337) calls addExercise for the substitute and does nothing at all to the exercise being replaced. The substitute joins as an ad-hoc exercise, so it renders in the added/freeform list at the bottom rather than in the replaced exercise's slot, and the original stays in the program list still un-done.

IMPORTANT — the user also asked whether the program is wrongly coupled to today's workout. IT IS NOT. The comment at SessionScreen.tsx:317-320 states the intent: "A substitute is performed-side only: it joins this session as an ad-hoc exercise and the program day keeps the exercise it planned." Swapping never mutates the program, which is correct and should stay that way. So this is NOT the bigger architectural bug the user feared — it is a narrower session-presentation bug. The performed-side-only design is right; what is missing is any record that the substitute REPLACED something, so the UI cannot render it as a replacement.

THE ACTUAL GAP: a swap currently produces "original (un-done) + substitute (ad-hoc, at the bottom)" when it should produce "substitute, in the original's position, with the original visibly stood down". Nothing in the data says the two are related. Compounding it, an un-done original means the day never reads as finished and StartScreen's client-side rotation advance stalls — the same symptom as T-042, reachable by a second route.

TO SETTLE:
- How is the replacement recorded? A per-(session, exercise) "replaced by" link is the honest model and lives on the session, never on the program. Note CLAUDE.md's rule that there is deliberately no session-exercise join table ("exercises belong to a session iff they have >=1 logged set") — a swap is the second feature (with T-042) that wants session-scoped per-exercise state, so design the two together rather than inventing two different mechanisms.
- What happens to sets already logged against the original before the swap? They are real work and must survive; the original cannot simply vanish from history.
- Does the substitute inherit the original's target sets/reps/rest and its position in program order? It should, or the swap is not really a substitute.
- Is a swap reversible mid-session?
- Interaction with supersetGroup: swapping one member of a superset must keep the pairing intact.

RELATED: T-042 (finish an exercise early) — both need session-scoped per-exercise state; solve the storage shape once for both.
title: Swapping should replace the exercise in today's session, not append to it
